questions.q: Choose the correct inversion of: “He seldom goes to the cinema.”
opts: Seldom he goes to the cinema.
Seldom does he go to the cinema.
Seldom does he goes to the cinema.
Seldom goes he to the cinema.
questions.why: Negative adverb first, then 'does' + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “____ is knocking at the door?”
questions.why: 'Who' is the subject of 'is knocking'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “She sang a beautiful song.”
opts: A beautiful song was sang by her.
A beautiful song is sung by her.
A beautiful song was sung by her.
A beautiful song has been sung by her.
questions.why: Past simple passive: was + past participle ('sung'). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Each of the students ____ given a certificate.”
questions.why: 'Each of' takes a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The surgeon decided to ____ the operation until the patient was stable.”
questions.why: 'Put off' means to postpone. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “They say that he is honest.”
opts: It is said him to be honest.
He was said to be honest.
He is said to be honest.
questions.why: Report-verb passive: subject + is said + to-infinitive. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “If I ____ a bird, I would fly to you.”
questions.why: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons in the if-clause. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “The train ______ before we reached the station.”
questions.why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Rina is the ____ girl in her class.” (tall)
questions.why: Superlative of a short adjective takes -est. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of “Alas” in: “Alas! The patient could not be saved.”
questions.why: 'Alas' expresses sudden emotion. GPSC-style practice item.
